summary: Image, chart and map labels in eight Malta regulator annual reports read by eye (cropped at 150-300 dpi, each checked against printed totals), Appendix B of the 2019-2020 report transcribed (135 recipients), items that had no indicator recorded with eight proposed indicators, the 2019-2020 rules added, and year columns that repeat earlier reports recorded under each source. A table-by-table and number-by-number check found further gaps beyond the listed to_do items; the table gaps were extracted, the rest are listed in each ledger to_do.

observations.location: PDF p. 17 (printed p. 12), section 3.2 Human Resources
observations.quote: The IIP unit is currently composed of seven employees
observations.notes: Staff of the IIP unit within Identity Malta at the time of writing (report dated October 2014).

observations.quote: the IIP's foreign direct investment comprising deposits, bonds, medical insurance, and real estate among other elements, equates to almost €10million per week
observations.notes: Concessionaire Henley & Partners' statement (10 June 2014) as reported by the regulator: a weekly rate of 'foreign direct investment' from the IIP ('almost'); scale million. The regulator adds that not all investment had materialised (PQ 9874).

observations.quote: from each approved applicant, the economy stands to gain €1.67 million in nominal growth, additional to that planned from the IIP
observations.notes: A local economist's estimate (15 February 2014) quoted by the regulator; per approved applicant; scale million. Same quotation gives 75,000 jobs (already recorded as rbi_jobs_created).

observations.period: each of the three years to the cap (estimate of 15 Feb 2014)
observations.quote: If 600 applications are approved each year for three years until the capping is reached, the total additional nominal GDP expansion could exceed €1 billion for each of these three years
observations.notes: A local economist's estimate (15 February 2014) quoted by the regulator, assuming 600 approvals a year for three years; printed as a lower bound ("could exceed"); scale billion.

new_indicators.name: Agents through whom applications were submitted
new_indicators.definition: Licensed agents (intermediaries) through whom the applications decided, vetted or submitted in a period were filed, as counted by the source. Breakdown category= for groups the source defines (e.g. the busiest agents, agents with all or none of their applications approved, agents by number of applications submitted). Not the number of licensed agents (agents_licensed).
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-mlt-images-2026-10-10 for the Malta regulator's "Agents' Performance" statistics (2019-2020 report, p. 12).

new_indicators.name: Share of applications submitted by a group of agents
new_indicators.definition: Percentage of the applications decided, vetted or submitted in a period that were filed through a stated group of agents (category=, e.g. the four busiest agents), as printed. Never calculated by us.

new_indicators.name: Outcome rate of an agent's applications
new_indicators.definition: Percentage of the applications filed through one agent (or a stated agent within a group) that ended with a stated outcome, category= approved or not_approved (with the agent group in the category name), as printed. Agents are not named in the breakdown.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-mlt-images-2026-10-10 (Malta regulator, 2019-2020 report: best and worst of the four busiest agents; one firm's agent under review).

new_indicators.name: Share of licensed agents by type
new_indicators.definition: Percentage of the agents licensed or accredited by the programme authority at a date that belong to one type of firm or profession (category=), as printed. Counts are agents_licensed.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-mlt-images-2026-10-10 (Malta regulator tables of agents by type, 2017-2024).

new_indicators.name: Cases on which the programme agency worked with the financial intelligence unit
new_indicators.definition: Programme cases on which the programme agency collaborated with the financial intelligence unit in a period, other than cases it reported itself (those are cbi_suspicious_transaction_reports), as stated.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-mlt-images-2026-10-10 (Malta regulator, 2019-2020 report p. 16: 51 cases).

new_indicators.name: Requests for review of a refusal
new_indicators.definition: Complaints or requests for review of a refused programme application lodged with the authority or regulator that reviews refusals, in a period or cumulatively; empty breakdown = received; category=investigated, accepted or refused for what the reviewer did with them, as printed.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-mlt-images-2026-10-10 (Malta regulator: IIP requests for review and 2020-scheme complaints, 2019-2020 to 2024 reports).

new_indicators.name: Persons naturalised without a stated document
new_indicators.definition: Persons naturalised through a programme who, according to the source, did not provide a stated document (category=, e.g. birth_certificate). Usually a claim; not a finding that the naturalisation was irregular.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-mlt-images-2026-10-10 (an MP's claim of 58 IIP citizens without their own birth certificate, relayed in the 2019-2020 regulator report).

new_indicators.name: Entities receiving applicant donations
new_indicators.definition: Number of local entities (charities, NGOs, cultural, sport or other bodies) that received donations from programme applicants in a period or cumulatively, as printed. Breakdown category= for groups by number of donations received. Amounts and numbers of donations are cbi_applicant_donations.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-mlt-images-2026-10-10 (Malta regulator reports 2019-2020 to 2024).
